text:
Evan Rodrigues won two Stanley Cups in Florida and is now a Devil, and his last two games were a reminder of why teams keep wanting him: four points against Washington, including a power-play goal on Nov. 12 and two more goals in a 7-4 win on Nov. 14. He has six goals and 11 points in 21 games on about 15 minutes a night.

The goals are running ahead of the chances. He has six on 3.9 expected, shooting 17.6% against a range closer to 12%, and his own chance rate is a bit below last season's. His overall scoring rate sits at the top of our talent range, so some cooling is likely.

At five on five, New Jersey is about even with him on the ice but seven points worse than without him, which is the part to watch. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking credits him with clean breakouts (64% of exits with possession) and lots of attempts, though fewer from the slot than his volume suggests. The goals have come at useful times, too: our wins added measure rates his clutch scoring well above his chances.
